sara: Heads up — after the runtime roll (runtimes/v2.14) we're seeing a regression on Mistral-12B configs with non‑standard head dims. p50 doubled for small seq (64) and p95 has big tail.
sara: Quick numbers from canary: p50 30ms -> 68ms, p95 110ms -> 420ms, throughput down ~35%.
sara: Logs show a ton of kernel fallback churn: FlashAttention -> SDPA -> Triton slowpath repeatedly for the same request.
jun: ugh. any pattern by head-dim? which model variant?
sara: It's the odd-head variant we onboarded (head_dim=48) — Mixtral/Mistral family. Llama configs with 64/80 are fine.
marco: 48 is not multiple of 8/16 so flash is supposed to fallback, but fallback shouldn't thrash compile cache. Did we change kernel selection order in v2.14?
sara: We moved Triton compile to lazy / on-demand which should reduce compile spikes, but profiling shows recompile attempts + cache eviction on the hot path.
ellie: throwing profiler dump:
```
# sample profile (canary host)
requests: 1200
avg_latency_ms: 68
kernel_switches_per_req: 4.2
fallback_events: flash->sdpa: 680, sdpa->triton: 420
triton_compile_time_ms: 240 avg per compile
triton_cache_evictions: 120
```
marco: 240ms per compile is the killer. Why are we compiling at runtime for the same shape repeatedly? cache key mismatch?
jun: I saw a cache key normalized by (head_dim, seq_len, dtype, mask_pattern). Maybe mask pattern uses pointer addresses for mask buffer if we changed mask pooling — could be non-deterministic.
sara: Stack traces show mask buffer ptr included in compile key sometimes. 
marco: That explains churn. If mask pointer leaks into the key, each request looks unique -> compile thrash -> slowpath.
ellie: Repro script (local):
```
for i in 1..500:
  curl -X POST /v1/models/mistral-12b/outputs -d '{"input":"hi","max_tokens":8}'
  sleep 0.01
done
```
ellie: Under 48-head config this creates ~200 unique compile keys in our trace.
jun: quick mitigation: force kernel selection to prefer precompiled SDPA when head_dim % 8 != 0 and avoid triton compile on the request path. We can also pin compile cache to longer TTL.
sara: Can we do a canary patch to short-circuit triton compile if compile_count > 1 in Xs window and fall back to the SDPA slow kernel?
marco: Yes. Add heuristic: if repeated compile attempts for same (model_id, head_dim, seq_bucket) within 60s, mark key as "compile-unstable" and route to fallback kernel.
jun: And we should fix mask keying — normalize mask metadata instead of pointer. I'll open a PR to strip buffer pointers from compile keys.
ellie: Also noticed KV-cache alignment issues for head_dim 48: our kv prefetch stride assumed 64B alignment which sometimes misreads tail elements causing additional copies and mask adjustments. Might be adding overhead.
sara: Good catch. That could amplify latency as we copy into aligned buffers.
marco: Action list: 1) JUN: PR to normalize compile keys (mask ptr removal) 2) MARCO: hotfix heuristic to mark compile-thrash and route to SDPA 3) ELLIE: KV prefetch alignment patch and microbench 4) SARA: run 10k request canary and collect p50/p95.
jun: I'll target PR today. If we get mask key fix + sdpa short-circuit, we should drop p95 dramatically.
sara: If anyone can help validate, please join the canary run in eu-west-1. I'll start an instance at 1745625000.
runtime-bot: deploy-status: rollout v2.14.1-hotfix started for mistral-oddheads -> canary cluster. :rocket:
marco: noted. after hotfix I'll run the tracer and post a flamegraph.
ellie: also adding a small unit test to ensure compile key components are deterministic (no pointers).
sara: Thanks all — priority P0 for the next 24h. ping me if p95 resurfaces. :)
